description: BlackICe is building Field Shift to help smallholder farmers compare crop rotations using NASA climate data, Sentinel-2 imagery, crop suitability information and soil sensors. We bring software development skills and a practical focus on farmers in Kenya, including access through basic phones. Join us if you enjoy agriculture, Earth observation, IoT, data analysis, design or storytelling. We especially welcome agronomy and hardware expertise.
summary:
Field Shift is a decision-support prototype that helps smallholder farmers explore crop rotation options using satellite information, farm conditions and documented agricultural guidance. Developed by Team BlackICe for the Kisumu Local Event, it focuses on a demonstration area near Muhoroni, Kenya.

The prototype retrieves historical temperature and rainfall from NASA POWER and GPM IMERG, combines them with FAO/IIASA GAEZ crop suitability information, and presents rotation discussion examples supported by KALRO guidance. Farmers can enter crop history, water access, soil information and priorities, then compare options with visible evidence and limitations.

A working soil-device simulator sends clearly labelled synthetic measurements through an authenticated backend into a monitoring dashboard. A Sentinel-2 processing adapter is implemented, with live retrieval awaiting configuration and verification. An SMS simulator demonstrates access for farmers without smartphones.

Field Shift makes scattered information easier to understand while preserving uncertainty. It supports informed discussion with agricultural advisers rather than promising yields or replacing professional advice.
details:
Field Shift helps smallholder farmers explore crop rotation options by bringing environmental history, modelled crop suitability, farmer knowledge and documented agronomic guidance into one accessible workflow.

THE PROBLEM

Choosing what to plant after a harvest requires information about previous crops, water availability, soil conditions, growing periods and crop compatibility. These inputs are often scattered across different sources. Farmers without smartphones face additional barriers to accessing and interpreting digital information.

HOW IT WORKS

A farmer or assisting officer creates a farm profile, confirms its location, and records crop history, soil information, irrigation access, planting intentions and priorities. Unknown information remains explicitly unknown.

The application retrieves daily temperature and GPM IMERG rainfall through NASA POWER. It displays historical observations with their dates, units, sources and missing-data status. These observations provide regional context and are not presented as forecasts or direct farm measurements.

The prototype includes an extracted FAO/IIASA GAEZ v4 suitability subset for the grid cell containing the public Muhoroni demonstration point. It represents the 1981–2010, rain-fed, low-input, current-cropland scenario. Other locations and incompatible scenarios remain unknown.

Documented KALRO guidance supports maize–bean and maize–cowpea rotation discussion examples. The application explains supporting evidence, constraints and missing information without inventing yield, profit or suitability scores. Saved plans preserve the information and assumptions used when they were created.

SATELLITE AND SOIL MONITORING

Sentinel-2 is a core component of the intended system. A Copernicus Data Space adapter has been implemented for scene discovery, quality screening, imagery and NDVI processing. Live retrieval has not yet been verified because provider configuration is outstanding. NDVI is treated as vegetation information, not proof of nutrient status, crop identity or soil health.

A standalone virtual soil device generates deterministic, synthetic moisture and temperature readings. It sends them through an authenticated ingestion API into a local database. The system demonstrates validation, duplicate handling, credential revocation and clearly labelled monitoring. No physical sensor performance or calibration has been validated.

ACCESSIBILITY AND INCLUSION

The responsive web interface supports farmers and assisted planning. English and Kiswahili farmer workflows are included, with translations awaiting human review. An interactive SMS simulator demonstrates a basic-phone journey; live SMS delivery is not connected.

TECHNOLOGY

The project uses React, Vite, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS and Recharts for the frontend; Cloudflare Workers for APIs; local Cloudflare D1 for monitoring records; Python for GAEZ extraction; and a TypeScript device simulator. Automated verification includes unit tests, browser tests and local ingestion checks.

CREATIVITY AND INTENDED IMPACT

Field Shift connects regional space observations with local farm information while making the origin and limitations of each observation visible. Its hardware-ready interface allows a virtual device to be replaced by physical equipment without redesigning the ingestion contract.

The intended impact is to make crop-planning evidence easier to access and discuss, including for farmers without smartphones. Agricultural review and farmer testing are still needed before real-world recommendations. Real authentication, live SMS, production deployment and broader geographic suitability coverage remain future work.
